text:
Marcus Reed: heads up on L40S stability from last night’s burst tests. we’re still seeing intermittent OOMs when we push mixed prefill/decode at higher conc.

Rough repro:
- L40S 48GB, runtime-1.22 rc
- model: 13B chat (fp16), ctx 8k/16k mix
- conc >= 14 (with current defaults) + long-prefill tail => boom within 10-20 min
- doesn’t always repro in steady-state decode-heavy; seems tied to prefill spikes + fragmentation

Anyone have eyes on the last benchmark-lab runs? want to propose a headroom bump for L40S profile before we re-run.

Omar El-Sayed: yep, I pulled the GPU mem traces from the canary pool. it’s not a single allocation spike; it’s creeping reserved + allocator fragmentation. pattern:
- `gpu_mem_reserved` climbs to ~46.5–47.2GB
- then a prefill request tries to grab a contiguous block for KV growth / workspace and fails
- we get `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation` and the runtime kills the model worker

Two notes:
1) compaction counters show we’re compacting, but compaction time jumps right before the OOM (probably thrashing)
2) fragmentation estimate (the new heuristic) sits around 0.18–0.25 in the “bad” window

Samir Qureshi: +1. L40S allocator is way less forgiving than H100 for our workload mix. we’re leaving too little slack for:
- transient prefill workspace (attention kernels)
- CUDA graph pools (if enabled)
- fragmentation overhead
- driver/runtime overhead (varies w/ driver)

I’d like to set explicit *required headroom* in the L40S profile and enforce it via admission control.

Proposed starting point (safe default): keep >= 7GB free (so cap usable at ~41GB) → ~14–15% headroom.

In profile-pack terms (naming bikeshed):
- `memory.headroom_fraction: 0.15`
- `kv_cache.max_bytes_fraction: 0.72` (current is 0.80-ish)
- plus reduce peak concurrent prefills (separate from overall concurrency)

Lena Fischer: what were the request shapes when it died? (prompt length / output length). if it’s long-prefill + short outputs, then our scheduler is letting too many prefills pile up.

I’m worried we’re “fixing” it purely w/ headroom but still leaving the underlying prefill burst issue.

Sofia Ivanova: scheduler side: L40S currently uses the same bucket policy as H100 (minus some caps), which is probably too optimistic. in mixed traffic, prefill can dominate queue and inflate memory pressure.

We can try two changes in next rerun:
- cap prefill in-flight tokens (or cap in-flight prefill requests) lower on L40S
- more aggressive backpressure when queueing_ms > threshold (avoid prefill burst)

But I agree with Samir: we need a headroom floor regardless.

Yuki Sato: on the kernel path, L40S is hitting fallback more often for long context. not directly OOM-causing, but fallback kernels sometimes allocate bigger temp buffers.

Can we add a per-profile guard: disable the larger-temp variant for L40S when ctx > 8k? (or at least count it + correlate)

Allison Grant: can you all drop metric names you’re looking at so we can add a panel to the Runtime Profiles dashboard? specifically want:
- OOM rate by `profile_id`
- `gpu_mem_allocated`/`reserved` (p95/p99)
- fragmentation estimate
- compaction time
- scheduler queueing_ms

(also reminder: cardinality. please don’t tag on raw model_id if we can avoid it.)

Omar El-Sayed: metrics we’re using right now:
- `runtime_gpu_mem_allocated_bytes{sku,profile_id}`
- `runtime_gpu_mem_reserved_bytes{sku,profile_id}`
- `runtime_kv_compaction_ms{sku,profile_id}` (hist)
- `runtime_fragmentation_estimate{sku,profile_id}` (gauge)
- `runtime_oom_total{sku,profile_id,stage}` (stage is prefill/decode/model_load)

We *don’t* have a clean “largest free block” metric; fragmentation_estimate is our proxy.

Marcus Reed: numbers from last run (approx):
- stable at conc=12
- flaky at conc=14
- basically guaranteed OOM at conc=16 with long-prefill mixed in

At conc=14, `reserved` hovers 46.8GB, sometimes spikes 47.1GB, then dies.

If we hold 7GB headroom, reserved should never exceed ~41GB, so we should have buffer.

Vanessa Ortiz: infra note: L40S fleet has some driver variance still (we’re in the middle of standardizing). a couple nodes on newer driver showed worse reserved growth.

So please don’t assume “works on one node” == good. Rerun matrix needs at least 3 nodes across the two driver baselines.

Irene Choi: +1, and we have some PCIe topology differences (not NUMA nightmares, but enough to change CPU-side overhead). for stability, headroom + admission control is safer than “just” tuning scheduling.

Rina Kobayashi: I can schedule reruns in benchmark-lab tonight.

Need a concrete set of profile changes and the matrix slice:
- models: 7B + 13B (fp16) + 13B (int8?)
- ctx buckets: 2k, 8k, 16k
- conc sweep: 8/10/12/14
- traffic: mixed prefill/decode distribution (same seed)

Also: do we want to include a “burst prefill” stress test (N prefills back-to-back) as a gating case?

Samir Qureshi: yes on burst stress test. that’s the closest to real prod incidents.

Concrete proposal for L40S profile v1.0.1 (names tbd):

```yaml
profiles:
  - id: l40s-default
    sku: L40S
    memory:
      headroom_fraction: 0.15
      allocator:
        large_alloc_warn_fraction: 0.90
    kv_cache:
      max_bytes_fraction: 0.72
      compaction:
        enable: true
        target_fragmentation: 0.12
        max_compaction_ms_per_min: 250
    scheduler:
      max_concurrency: 12
      max_inflight_prefill_requests: 3
      queue:
        max_queue_ms: 40
```

Key point: `max_concurrency=12` default. allow override upward but only w/ explicit “unsafe” flag.

(reactions: :thumbsup: x3)

Lena Fischer: I like having separate prefill cap. in our current implementation, `max_concurrency` alone doesn’t prevent prefill bursts.

One question: does `max_inflight_prefill_requests: 3` tank throughput for small prompts? might be fine but we should measure tokens/sec impact.

Sofia Ivanova: agree. for L40S, we can accept a bit less peak throughput if it keeps p99 stable and prevents worker churn.

Also for queue policy: if `max_queue_ms=40` is too tight, we’ll start rejecting early. Might be OK for Hosted but Dedicated customers might prefer queueing over 429s. we should align w/ dedicated defaults (maybe keep Hosted strict, Dedicated less strict but same headroom).

Yuki Sato: if we change kernel variant behavior, I can do a follow-up, but for this rerun let’s just instrument kernel fallback rate and correlate with OOM windows.

Allison Grant: ok, I’ll draft a dashboard panel spec with:
- `runtime_oom_total` + overlay `runtime_gpu_mem_reserved_bytes`
- `runtime_fragmentation_estimate` + compaction_ms
- fallback rate per `kernel_choice`

If you can tag the rerun results with `profile_version=l40s-1.0.1-candidate` that’ll make comparison easier.

Rina Kobayashi: cool. can you all land the config change behind the L40S profile flag and ping me with the commit hash? cutoff for tonight’s lab window is ~18:00 PT.

Marcus Reed: I’ll put together a PR with the proposed headroom + conc/prefill caps (no scheduler algorithm changes yet). will ping when it’s up.

Omar El-Sayed: I’ll double-check the kv_cache fraction math to ensure we’re not double-counting headroom (kv_cache cap + allocator reserve). last thing we want is “too conservative” because we stacked caps.

Vanessa Ortiz: please include driver version in the benchmark metadata output if it’s not already. we keep losing time on “why is node A different”.

Marcus Reed: ack. Rina, I’ll add driver/CUDA to benchmark tags if it’s missing.

benchmark-lab-bot: Scheduled run request created by @Rina Kobayashi: matrix=l40s_stability_v2, start=1768844300, nodes=3, tags=profile_version:l40s-1.0.1-candidate

Sofia Ivanova: once we have rerun results, we should decide whether L40S default conc is 12 hard cap vs “12 recommended”. I’m leaning hard cap for Hosted (we own it) and “recommended + guardrails” for Private.

Samir Qureshi: +1. also please add a note to expected behavior doc: “if you raise conc above 12 on L40S, expect increased OOM risk unless headroom >= 15% and prefill cap configured.”

Marcus Reed: cool. I’ll update this thread when the reruns finish.
